A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Squeezed Attention and provide readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench, RULER, and PreFixQA evaluations, GPU latency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds model evaluations, a clustering-granularity ablation, hierarchical lookup timings, and offline clustering measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions use normalized-key K-means clustering, centroid-based importance estimates, global thresholding, hierarchical retrieval, and exact attention over selected keys. v3 documents hierarchical kernels and grouped-query execution without establishing a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: LongBench, RULER, PreFixQA, and PG-19 workloads are retained. PreFixQA still contains 47 documents and 1,127 question-answer pairs. Added models and ablations over existing LongBench tasks do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: QUEST remains the LongBench comparator, including for the added models. Full-KV, ideal-lookup, and FlashAttention/FlashDecoding controls are retained; newly discussed prefill methods are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-3.1-8B and Falcon3-7B evaluations with grouped-query attention, independently selected keys per query head, and profiled KV budgets. New protocols vary centroid counts and pruning, benchmark hierarchical lookup at 90% first-level and greater than 90% second-level sparsity, and time 128K clustering on eight H100 NVL GPUs. Existing accuracy protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 7 tests clustering granularity against pruning aggressiveness; Table 9 isolates hierarchical lookup costs; Table 10 measures offline preparation costs. These substantially expand analysis of the hierarchy's motivation and practical overheads. Existing t-SNE, attention-skewness, ideal-lookup, and kernel-optimization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Timing practices remain 100 warmup and 500 measurement runs for prefill, and 50 measurements for each of 100 query tokens during generation, relocated to v3 Appendix F. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Original accuracy Tables 2–4, ideal-lookup results, kernel ablation values, and latency charts are unchanged. v3 adds model scores in Table 5, granularity-dependent accuracy in Table 7, hierarchical lookup speedups of 1.22x and 1.41x in Table 9, and offline preparation times of 23 and 24 minutes in Table 10. These are new experimental results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 removes the explicit fractional-retention assumption 0 < p < 1 and describes c' as clusters retrieved per level rather than clusters used before fractional pruning. The O(c' log L + k) bound and Equations 1–3 remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows one hierarchical-complexity claim from per-token generation to centroid lookup. The main method and benchmark contributions, 3.1x/8x KV-budget claims, and 4.3x/4.2x prefill/decode speedup claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 Section 8 adds the limitation that less-important keys receive no approximation to compensate for their omission. Appendix G discusses greater accuracy degradation on Llama-3.1 and possible aggregation across query heads sharing KV entries. Existing fixed-context and hyperparameter limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 explains the previously mentioned 100-token threshold calibration, hierarchical GPU kernel indexing and workload balancing, grouped-query KV-budget profiling, and clustering hardware and timing components. It also distinguishes metadata storage from loading overhead. These fill important implementation gaps; the code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds positioning against prefill sparsity approaches, citing MInference and PyramidInfer, and v3 adds a Falcon3 reference. The Triton introduction reference is removed. Most earlier related work is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially condensed and reorganized. Detailed related work, kernel descriptions, dataset curation, and experimental settings are consolidated in appendices; accuracy subsections are merged, and limitations move into the main text. Abstract and contribution prose are also revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables and shortening table labels. v1's PreFixQA example Figure 4 is removed, while v3 adds Tables 5, 7, 9, and 10. Existing method diagrams and diagnostic plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful validation and transparency through grouped-query model evaluations, the granularity ablation, previously unreported hierarchical and offline costs, and clearer calibration details. These improve assessment of applicability and implementation choices. The gains remain bounded: hierarchical latency measurements use different pruning settings from the retained accuracy evaluation, so they do not fully establish a joint accuracy-speed tradeoff.
